checks: No eclipse at 76 of 225 covered epochs where the 0.68704 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 258204238 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.6870 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 1.13 percent, with a very strong detection signal-to-noise ratio of 692.6 in the box least-squares periodogram search. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 13.5, though the centroid shows a 2.2 arcsecond offset from the catalog position. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. This candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate from the automated pipeline. The machine-learning classifier assigns it a score of 0.45, indicating moderate likelihood of being a real eclipsing system rather than an instrumental artifact or false positive.
